question: In React 19, what happens if a ref callback returns a function?
options: React ignores the returned value
React calls the function on every render
React calls that function as cleanup when the element is detached, instead of calling the ref with null
React throws because ref callbacks must return undefined
explanation: Ref callbacks can now return a cleanup function, similar to effects.

subject: react
question: Why does a state variable that holds a function need useState(() => fn) instead of useState(fn)?
options: Functions cannot be stored in state at all
It avoids creating a closure
useState calls a function argument as an initializer, so fn would be called and its return value stored
useState(fn) makes the state read-only
explanation: A function passed to useState is treated as a lazy initializer, and the same applies to setState updaters.

subject: react
question: A custom hook returns an object literal { value, setValue } on every render. What problem can this create?
options: The hook's state is shared between components
setValue stops working after the first render
React throws because hooks cannot return objects
Consumers that put the returned object in effect dependencies or memo props see a new reference every render
explanation: Unless memoized, the object identity changes each render, which can retrigger effects or break memoization.

subject: react
question: Why does moving frequently changing state down into a small child component often improve performance?
options: Only that child and its descendants re-render when the state changes, not its former siblings
It turns the state into a ref
React skips rendering children of stateful components
It enables server rendering for the parent
explanation: State updates re-render the owning component's subtree, so keeping state close to where it is used shrinks that subtree.

subject: react
question: Why does a component written as const Item = memo(function Item(props) {...}) still show as Item in React DevTools?
options: memo copies the variable name at runtime
React reads the file name
DevTools reads the name of the inner named function
DevTools always shows Memo instead
explanation: Naming the function passed to memo or forwardRef gives the component a useful display name in DevTools and error stacks.

subject: react
question: Why might splitting state and dispatch into two separate contexts improve performance?
options: It removes the need for a reducer
dispatch changes on every render
React allows only one value per context
Components that only dispatch do not re-render when the state changes, because dispatch is stable
explanation: dispatch from useReducer has a stable identity, so a context holding only dispatch never triggers re-renders.

subject: react
question: Why can't a Client Component import a Server Component module directly?
options: React throws when two components share a name
Imported modules become part of the client bundle, so the Server Component would run as client code; pass it as children instead
Server Components have no default export
Client Components cannot render JSX
explanation: Server Components can be passed to Client Components as props like children, which keeps them rendered on the server.

subject: react
question: What does useSyncExternalStore require from the getSnapshot function?
options: It must return a new object every call
It must return a cached value that stays identical by Object.is while the store has not changed
It must be async
It must subscribe to the store
explanation: Returning a fresh object each time makes React think the store changed on every render, causing an infinite loop.

subject: react
question: Why might onClick on a parent div fire after a React portal child is clicked, even though the portal renders elsewhere in the DOM?
options: React re-dispatches every click globally
Portals copy event listeners to the body
Browsers bubble events to every div
Events in portals propagate through the React tree, not the DOM tree
explanation: A portal stays a child of its React parent, so synthetic events bubble to React ancestors.

subject: react
question: In React 19, a form uses action={submit} where submit is a Server Function. What happens if JavaScript has not loaded yet when the user submits?
options: The form can still submit as a regular form post when used with a framework that supports progressive enhancement
The browser shows an error
The data is silently lost
Nothing happens until hydration completes in all cases
explanation: Server Function form actions can work before hydration, which is a key benefit of progressive enhancement.
